text:
The translation captures the basic imagery but suffers from several issues. "The sash gradually widened" is overly literal and misses the metonymy—the sash loosens because the speaker has wasted away from longing. The second line, "For the one who withered away for her sake," introduces grammatical ambiguity (it reads as if a third party withered) and over-translates "憔悴" (haggard/emaciated) as "withered away," which implies death rather than lovesick deterioration. A more polished version might be: "Though my belt grows loose, I never regret / For her, I have grown haggard and worn." The response is functional but lacks the sophistication and precision requested.

Rating: [[5]]
